questions.stem: What are the products when sodium reacts with water?
questions.explanation: When sodium reacts with water, it produces sodium hydroxide (an alkali) and hydrogen gas: 2Na + 2H₂O → 2NaOH + H₂. The sodium hydroxide dissolves, making the solution alkaline. This is why Group 1 elements are called 'alkali metals'.

questions.stem: Why does reactivity increase going down Group 1?

options.text: The atoms get smaller, making them more reactive
The outer electron is closer to the nucleus
The outer electron is further from the nucleus with more shielding, so it is lost more easily
The atoms gain more outer electrons

questions.explanation: Going down Group 1, atoms have more electron shells, so the outer electron is further from the nucleus. There is also more shielding from inner electrons. This means there is less attraction between the nucleus and the outer electron, so it is lost more easily, increasing reactivity.
